ISOMORPHISM CLAUSE. Source (sm-3:361-365): "A named record isomorphism is a bijection Φ : M → M' preserving successor, pairing, over/under bits and these signs. The parametrizing circles are oriented; the finite bijection must preserve their cyclic orders. It does not prescribe a map at every unmarked parameter and does not permit traversal reversal." Lean `RecordIso` (LinkRecord.lean:539-552) has `Φ : ρ.M ≃ ρ'.M`, `succ_eq : ∀ v, Φ (ρ.succ v) = ρ'.succ (Φ v)` (Φ∘s = s'∘Φ, never s'⁻¹, so reversal is excluded whenever |M| ≥ 3 and indistinguishable otherwise, exactly as for the printed finite bijection), `pair_eq`, `bit_eq`, `sgn_eq`, plus `e : ρ.comps ≃ ρ'.comps` and `comp_eq : ρ'.comp (Φ v) = e (ρ.comp v)`. For the printed one-circle case `comps = Fin 1`, `e` is unique and `comp_eq` is trivial, so RecordIso is exactly the printed bijection. For many circles, `Record.succ_comp` and `succ_cycle` (LinkRecord.lean:331-334) make the succ-cycles equal to the fibres of `comp`, so a succ-preserving Φ already induces the circle bijection on occupied circles; `e` only adds the matching of crossing-free circles (the rp:record-polynomial clause, a faithful extra outside this row's one-circle source). Attacks tried: (i) Φ exchanging the two circles of a two-component record with two mixed crossings and matching bits/signs — a RecordIso with e = swap in Lean, and a legitimate isomorphism under the document's multi-circle reading; (ii) a single-occurrence circle — impossible for any planar Diagram (each component carries 2 occurrences per self-crossing plus an even number of intersections with each other closed curve), and for abstract records `e` is forced by Φ on occupied circles; (iii) Φ preserving succ/pair/bits/signs but no `e` — only when the numbers of crossing-free circles differ, which the printed one-circle definition does not cover and rp:record-polynomial also rejects. No bijection was found that the printed text and the Lean classify differently in the printed setting. The `cyclic_order` field uses `VisitBetween v w u := cycBetween (visitCoord v) (visitCoord w) (visitCoord u)` (LinkDiagramRecord.lean:882-883), `cycBetween a b c := (a < b ∧ b < c) ∨ (b < c ∧ c < a) ∨ (c < a ∧ a < b)` (line 78-79), the same formula as the accepted `traversalBetween` (Traversal.lean:73-76) of def:gauss; it is restricted to triples on one circle (the only place the cyclic order is meaningful) and states the consequence of successor preservation (`RecordIso.visitBetween_iff`, `nextVisit_comm_iff_visitBetween_iff` give the equivalence). "Does not prescribe a map at every unmarked parameter" is structural: RecordIso contains no circle map.
